note: Power setpoint for the HEATING channel. Only the channel of the currently active mode carries a value; the other two sit at -100.0. -100.0 is the valid lower clamp of a live controller output ("this channel requests nothing"), NOT an error code. -127.0 IS an error code (invalid / no heat-generator demand, 30 % of all samples) and must be filtered out, otherwise consumers show a phantom -12.7 % request.
DHW channel. See dp 2040 for the -100 / -127 semantics.
Cooling channel. See dp 2040 for the -100 / -127 semantics.

Aggregate setpoint = whichever of dp 2040/2041/2042 belongs to the active mode. Verified: equals max(2040,2041,2042) in 6530 of 6587 samples (99.1 %); the 57 exceptions are read-time skew during ramps, all but one below 10 %. Ramps at roughly 0.5 %/min and reacts within one sample to a changed flow setpoint, so it is a useful EARLY INDICATOR that the compressor is about to start. It is NOT a start criterion: across 25 observed start/stop events the value ranged from -51 % to +100 %.
Despite Hoval's name "0-100% current req." this is BINARY: across 759 consecutive samples only 0 (no heating-circuit demand) and 100 (demand present) were ever observed.
